content.name: Qiyue Tang
content.aiIntroduction: The results collected here were generated with AI assistance and have not been fully verified by a human.
content.shortBio: I am a third-year undergraduate majoring in Mathematics and Applied Mathematics.
content.aiAboutBody:
The design of this interface was inspired by the personal homepage of Jihao Liu, an assistant professor at Peking University.

I began using AI to assist with my mathematical research in mid-August 2026. Recently, I have gradually obtained some results in areas that interest me. However, I am only an undergraduate, and my time and abilities are limited, so I cannot fully digest the results I have generated in a short period. Since I also wish to [large]**adhere to academic standards**[/large], I have set up this page.

I have recently posted a number of papers on Hexagon for the reasons described below. This page presents [highlight]only some of the more important results[/highlight] I have obtained. **I welcome criticism and suggestions from everyone.** These results have not been uploaded to arXiv.

Some of the papers I posted on Hexagon grew out of my own research interests. Others came about in three ways.

1. Some fellow students, knowing that I have experience using AI for mathematics, asked me to test what it could do in other areas of mathematics or to post on their behalf results they had obtained using AI. Examples include [Schmeisser’s Conjecture in Large Degree](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00162v1), [A Lower Bound for the Filling Area of the Circle](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00218v2), and [A Counterexample to the Realizability Conjecture for Surface Classes](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00489v1).

2. Some faculty members reached out to me to express their interest in seeing solutions to major mathematical problems or progress toward them. I shared the results I obtained on those problems. Examples include [Hall polynomials for representation-finite algebras](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00403v1), [Reduction of the Gorenstein symmetry conjecture to finite rings](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00397v2), and [Cartan determinants in finite representation type over arbitrary fields](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00392v2).

3. Some faculty members asked me to use my experience with AI to tackle mathematical problems that had been open for at least ten years.

In my view, **credit should go to those who truly understand and organize the work**, as well as to the AI systems and agents involved, such as Rethlas, Danus, Pharos, and Rethlas-OSV. If I merely used AI to obtain a major result in a field unfamiliar to me and could not even understand the resulting paper, **I should not receive credit**.

If you are interested in **working through and organizing these results**, please contact me. I will provide more detailed materials, and **if you complete that work, the credit will be yours**. If you **find any errors**, please let me know; I will **make corrections and update the materials promptly**.

publications.title: Equal Lagrange Numbers with Non-Isomorphic Band Graphs: A Counterexample to Schiffler's Problem 6.3
A Truncated Singular-Value Bound for Spectral Variation of Normal Matrices

aiResults.title: Quantum Laurent Positivity for Mutation-Acyclic Cluster Algebras
Theta Bases for Rank-Two Quantum Cluster Algebras of Geometric Type
aiResults.note: This paper completes and extends the rank-two comparison developed in [Gao’s doctoral thesis](https://doi.org/10.14711/thesis-991013340358203412).

aiResults.title: A note of refinements to an algebra of infinite little finitistic dimension
aiResults.note: This paper generalizes OpenAI’s result #198.

aiResults.title: A note on counterexamples to homological conjectures
aiResults.note: This paper generalizes OpenAI’s result #199.

aiResults.title: Finite quantum theta functions for skew-symmetrizable seeds
aiResults.note: Many details and parts of the exposition could still be expanded.

aiResults.title: Hall polynomials for representation-finite algebras
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles Ringel’s 1992 conjecture on the existence of Hall polynomials for representation-finite algebras over finite fields.

aiResults.title: Lefschetz coefficients of quantum theta functions
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles four conjectures: Davison–Mandel’s Conjectures 1.4 (Lefschetz coefficients of quantum theta functions), 2.17 (Lefschetz labels in scattering diagrams), and 3.13 (Lefschetz coefficients in broken-line expansions), together with the two-wall conjecture (Conjecture 3.12) in [Davison’s ICM 2026 survey](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.08004v1). I set out to answer one conjecture and was surprised when the AI produced arguments addressing all four in one go.

aiResults.title: Algebraicity of rank-two scattering wall functions
Equality of the Mirković–Vilonen and theta bases
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles Conjecture 6.9 in [Joel Kamnitzer’s ICM 2022 survey](https://doi.org/10.4171/ICM2022/132). The equality of the two bases also implies the results of [The Mirković–Vilonen basis and cluster pointedness](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00614v1) (Conjecture 6.6) and [Biperfectness of the theta basis of a maximal unipotent subgroup](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00603v1) (Question 6.5). The paper’s AI-use statement records how Rethlas-OSV caught substantive errors missed by earlier reviews, including errors that blocked the proof of the main theorem.

aiResults.title: Positive polytopes and the full Fock–Goncharov conjecture
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it gives a necessary and sufficient polytope criterion for the full Fock–Goncharov conjecture for principal-coefficient cluster varieties in characteristic zero. The original duality conjectures date to [Fock and Goncharov’s 2003 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311245v1).

aiResults.title: Disproof of minimum CAD existence for algebraic sets in dimensions $n\ge4$
Deterministic Polynomial-Time Factorization over Finite Fields
Equivalence of the Four-Variable Hessian and Planar Jacobian Conjectures
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it establishes an equivalence over the complex numbers between the remaining open cases of the two conjectures: the four-variable Hessian conjecture ([Meng, 2003](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0308035)) and the planar Jacobian conjecture ([Keller, 1939](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01695502)).

aiResults.title: Undecidability of Quiver Mutation Equivalence
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it answers a basic question in cluster theory: no algorithm can decide whether two arbitrary quivers are mutation-equivalent. This answers the first problem on slide 7 of [Fomin’s OPAC 2022 talk](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/slides/fomin.pdf#page=7).

aiResults.title: Positivity of Canonical Basis Multiplication in Modified Quantum Groups
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles Lusztig’s canonical-basis positivity conjecture (1993, Conjecture 25.4.2) for symmetric Cartan data.

aiResults.title: The singular-support characterization of Lusztig sheaves
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles the singular-support characterization of Lusztig sheaves for finite loop-free quivers, a problem stemming from Lusztig’s 1990 proposal.

aiResults.title: Lusztig's conjectures for $B_n$, $\widetilde B_n$, and $\widetilde C_n$
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles Lusztig’s conjectures P1–P15 (2003) in the finite and affine types treated here.

aiResults.title: Lusztig's sharp bound for Hecke algebras
aiResults.note: This paper makes progress on Lusztig’s sharp boundedness conjecture (2003, §13.4) for Hecke algebras.

aiResults.title: Almost all $k$-Markov numbers are unique
aiResults.note: This result was inspired by [William Y. Chen’s Almost all Markoff numbers are unique](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00281v2).

aiResults.title: Monomial Immanants of Totally Nonnegative Matrices
aiResults.note: This paper resolves [Stembridge’s 1992 conjecture (Conjecture 2.1)](https://doi.org/10.4153/CJM-1992-066-1) on the nonnegativity of monomial immanants of totally nonnegative matrices.

aiResults.title: Another Proof of Laurent Positivity for Generalized Cluster Algebras
aiResults.note: This paper gives a new proof of Laurent positivity for Chekhov–Shapiro generalized cluster algebras using finite algebras, Harder–Narasimhan factorization, and scattering diagrams.

aiResults.title: Another proof of Laurent positivity for skew-symmetric quantum cluster algebras
aiResults.note: This paper gives a new proof of Laurent positivity for skew-symmetric quantum cluster algebras using polynomial shuffle algebras and positive wall-crossing formulas.

aiResults.title: Another proof of quantum Laurent positivity, II
aiResults.note: This paper gives a new combinatorial proof of Laurent positivity for skew-symmetric quantum cluster algebras using graph flow cones and transportation polytopes.

aiResults.title: Broué's Abelian Defect Group Conjecture for 2-Blocks
aiResults.note: Partial result. If correct, this proves the case p = 2 of [Broué’s abelian defect group conjecture (1990)](https://numdam.org/item/AST_1990__181-182__61_0/).

aiResults.title: Positivity for Weighted Linear Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
The Quantum Kazhdan–Lusztig Conjecture for Quantum Loop Algebras
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles the quantum Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture for untwisted quantum loop algebras at non-root-of-unity parameters, in the form proposed by Hernandez (2002 preprint, published in 2004).

aiResults.title: The Humphreys support conjecture
aiResults.note: If correct, this proves [Humphreys’s 1997 support conjecture](https://doi.org/10.1090/amsip/004/05) for tilting modules in characteristic greater than the Coxeter number.

aiResults.title: Lusztig's Fourier matrix conjecture for finite noncrystallographic Coxeter groups
aiResults.note: If the result is correct, it settles the Fourier matrix conjecture for finite noncrystallographic Coxeter groups, concerning the Fourier matrices introduced by Lusztig in 1993–1994.

aiResults.title: A proof of the scheme-theoretic Humphreys conjectures
aiResults.note: If true, this proves the traditional and relative scheme-theoretic Humphreys conjectures in characteristic greater than every simple factor’s Coxeter number. These are Conjectures 3.6 and 3.7 in [Achar and Riche’s ICM 2026 survey (2025 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.05063).

aiResults.title: A proof of the Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas conjecture
aiResults.note: If correct, this proves the [Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas conjecture (2006 preprint, published 2008)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612668) on mixed Hodge polynomials of primitive-twisted GL(n) character varieties.

aiResults.title: A proof of Lusztig’s conjectures for extended affine Weyl groups
aiResults.note: This paper makes progress on Lusztig’s conjectures P1–P15 (2003) by treating extended affine Weyl groups with positive integer-valued weight functions.

aiResults.title: A proof of Lusztig's connectedness conjecture in finite type
aiResults.note: This paper makes progress on Lusztig’s left-cell connectedness conjecture (Katata, 1983) by treating finite Weyl groups with equal parameters.

aiResults.title: A proof of the HLRV conjecture
aiResults.note: If correct, this proves the [Hausel–Letellier–Rodriguez-Villegas conjecture (2008 preprint, published 2011)](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.2076) on mixed Hodge polynomials of generic semisimple GL(n) character varieties.
